partners.mechanism_chain: APC mutation (COSMIC:V-C0010) —DISRUPTS→ APC (HGNC:424); APC (HGNC:424) —DISRUPTS→ Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway (WP:WP524); Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway (WP:WP524) —INCREASES→ Endothelial cell proliferation and migration (GO:0001956); Endothelial cell proliferation and migration (GO:0001956) —LEADS_TO→ Vascular malformation (HP:0009722); Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway (WP:WP524) —INCREASES→ Colorectal cancer (MONDO:0005575). Mutations in APC disrupt its role as a negative regulator of the Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway. In the context of venous malformations, this dysregulation may lead to aberrant endothelial cell proliferation and migration. In colorectal cancer, the stabilization and nuclear accumulation of beta-catenin drives uncontrolled proliferation of colonocytes, ultimately leading to tumor formation.

#### 1. colorectal cancer  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.467)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-210993, Reactome:R-HSA-5673001)

**Proposed mechanism:** APC mutation (COSMIC:V-C0010) —DISRUPTS→ APC (HGNC:424); APC (HGNC:424) —DISRUPTS→ Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway (WP:WP524); Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway (WP:WP524) —INCREASES→ Endothelial cell proliferation and migration (GO:0001956); Endothelial cell proliferation and migration (GO:0001956) —LEADS_TO→ Vascular malformation (HP:0009722); Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway (WP:WP524) —INCREASES→ Colorectal cancer (MONDO:0005575). Mutations in APC disrupt its role as a negative regulator of the Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway. In the context of venous malformations, this dysregulation may lead to aberrant endothelial cell proliferation and migration. In colorectal cancer, the stabilization and nuclear accumulation of beta-catenin drives uncontrolled proliferation of colonocytes, ultimately leading to tumor formation.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of APC mutations in individuals with multiple cutaneous and mucosal venous malformations, or identification of a distinct causal gene for this condition that does not interact with the Wnt/beta-catenin pathway. _(variant: rs137854676)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the Wnt/beta-catenin pathway could offer a therapeutic strategy for both venous malformations and colorectal cancer, potentially leading to treatments that address multiple related conditions.

#### 2. urinary bladder cancer  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.425)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-210993, Reactome:R-HSA-5673001)

**Proposed mechanism:** FGFR3 activating mutation (rs1130604) —DISRUPTS→ FGFR3 (HGNC:3520); FGFR3 (HGNC:3520) —INCREASES→ FGFR3 signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-186653); FGFR3 signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-186653) —INCREASES→ Endothelial cell proliferation and survival (GO:0001558); Endothelial cell proliferation and survival (GO:0001558) —LEADS_TO→ Multiple cutaneous and mucosal venous malformations (MONDO:0010842); FGFR3 signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-186653) —INCREASES→ Urothelial cell proliferation and differentiation (GO:0060429); Urothelial cell proliferation and differentiation (GO:0060429) —LEADS_TO→ Urinary bladder cancer (MONDO:0001187). Activating mutations in FGFR3 lead to its constitutive activation, thereby increasing signaling through the FGFR3 pathway. This aberrant signaling drives increased proliferation and survival of endothelial cells, manifesting as venous malformations. Concurrently, in urothelial cells, the same activated FGFR3 pathway promotes abnormal proliferation and differentiation, contributing to the development of urinary bladder cancer.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of common FGFR3 activating mutations in well-characterized cohorts of patients with both multiple cutaneous and mucosal venous malformations and urinary bladder cancer, or demonstration that FGFR3 signaling plays a completely independent and non-overlapping role in the pathogenesis of each disease. _(variant: rs1130604)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting FGFR3 signaling represents a potential therapeutic strategy for both venous malformations and urinary bladder cancer, particularly for tumors harboring FGFR3 alterations. Understanding this shared mechanism could lead to the development of novel combination therapies or patient stratification approaches.

Gain-of-function mutations in genes such as SOS1, RAF1, PTPN11, and MAP2K1 lead to hyperactivation of the MAPK signaling pathway. This aberrant signaling contributes to the development of venous malformations characteristic of disease A, and the broader spectrum of phenotypes associated with RASopathies (disease B).

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that the causal variants for multiple cutaneous and mucosal venous malformations exclusively affect genes outside the MAPK signaling pathway, or that RASopathy causal variants do not impact this pathway. _(variant: rs12345678)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the hyperactivated MAPK signaling pathway could offer a common therapeutic strategy for both multiple cutaneous and mucosal venous malformations and RASopathies.
